newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan is credit card thief heaven, says MasterCard.
newsitem.headline: Japan is credit card thief heaven, says MasterCard.

text.p: Japan is the destination of choice in Asia for credit card thieves and counterfeiters because its laws on the issue are too lax, MasterCard International Vice President Stuart McDonald said in Tokyo on Thursday.

McDonald told a news conference that counterfeit credit cards accounted for some 60 percent of fraud committed in the Asian region and the worst abuse was in Japan where major credit card issuers lost $150 million in 1996.
He said unlike most Asian nations, credit card fraud was not a criminal offence in Japan, with offenders having to be pursued through long trials in civil courts.

Since possession of counterfeit or stolen cards is not a crime, police do not write reports on them. With no statistics to prove the extent of the problem, the government is under little pressure to criminalise the fraud through legislation.
McDonald urged Japan to follow neighbours like South Korea, Hong Kong and Malaysia which for years have punished credit card counterfeiting and fraud with jail terms.
"(Japan's) criminal legislation relating to card payment instruments needs to catch up with the 20th century, let alone the 21st," he said.
